title: RAW UNREVIEWED: OL/OR alternation marks free versus complement-taking nominal state in an identifying resumption
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_TESTED. Treat the OL/OR lattice as a possible nominal-state alternation, not a scale: a free head is resumed by a same-core relational head whose overt complement identifies the intended bearer. The written chor chol daiin sequence is a construction anchor only; none of its words is translated.

design.positive_structure: Directed composition, reusable core/carrier/wrapper cells and whole-form residuals motivate a shared construction with lexical restrictions. GDT629 owns the exact repeated three-group sequence; its old semantic labels are not evidence. GDT915 known-family transfer and mixed cells, and GDT916 failure on new stems, require lexical restrictions rather than universal agreement.
design.authoring_mechanism: A compiler introduces a nominal topic and then specifies which bearer is meant by repeating the same nominal core in a complement-taking form. This is a speculative production mechanism, not an independently attested Voynich language or proposed historical provenance.

anchor.limit: Existing primary report read, no target extraction. These are matching written spans in alternate readings of two manuscript sites, not confirmed clauses, independent translations or a five-token f38v rerun.

design.finite_content_construction: Anonymous nominal type X first introduces a topic x; a same-core relational nominal resumes x and binds it to an overt referent z: an X, specifically the X related to z. Rival property construction introduces x of type X and ascribes an independently valued property P to x. No value for X, P, z, daiin, a suffix or wrapper is selected.
design.orientation: Both OL-free/OR-dependent and OR-free/OL-dependent remain unassessed raw alternatives. No orientation may be picked from the anchor alone.
design.unequal_written_consequence: Under nominal-state resumption, the dependent form opens an obligatory nominal-complement slot and the free form does not; repetition retains the first head referent. The property rival does not create this dependency. Across another already-attested core, the same state orientation must bind a written complement rather than being changed to preserve a local story. A nominal-state account predicts identity between resumed heads, not an independently named material versus quality.
design.smallest_next_action: Author both bracketings for the two complete report-owned containing lines and a second already-owned family construction, using one head/resumption/complement rule. Before assigning any exact form a referent or function, retrieve its profile and retained contexts. Keep other words unknown and count them as unaccounted content; no whole-paragraph translation prerequisite is imposed. An absent complement is a contradiction only where the complete phrase boundary is actually fixed.
design.frequency_burden: The frequent final form may eventually be tested as a broadly reusable nominal/reference expression, but recurrence alone licenses no pronoun, article or numeral assignment. Standalone OL/OR and substrings stay separate.

likely_failure: The two forms may encode independent lexical meanings, phonological alternants or differently written words rather than nominal state.
The anchor can receive a vacuous identity paraphrase unless a genuine complement and its discourse relation are supplied.
OL/OR forms at demonstrable phrase boundaries may contradict obligatory complementation.
All grammatical values remain unassessed; this raw alternative is not a supported reading and does not establish a source language.
design.access: Route, composition topic, bounded duplicate search and existing GDT629/945/946 primary reports only. No target payload extraction, new image, reserve, fit, decoder or GDT1167 annotation access.
